name: pi-antiloop
description: Antiloop: detect reasoning loops and force a break (warn → force → abort) across text, tool, thinking, structural, and intra-message degenerate-repetition patterns (a model stuck emitting the same word hundreds of times inside ONE message or bash call, e.g. a 46 KB username list repeating lorem ×5145). Degenerate bash is blocked before it executes; a degenerate message is caught at message_end — no repeated peer needed. The force break is delivered mid-run: a real break message is steered into the running agent right before its next LLM call, and if the model ignores it and keeps repeating verbatim, antiloop aborts the run — an autonomous tool loop always terminates. Tool-loop detection is result-aware: only near-identical repeated calls with the same outcome count, so sequential bash operations and retries that make progress don’t false-positive. Task-stream recognition: when an extension (punched, plan, …) makes the model call the SAME tool many times with DIFFERENT content — N distinct tasks of one type, e.g. appending lines or adding plan tasks — antiloop stays silent.
author: antiloop contributors <https://github.com/noguerol>
